summary: Cart user_id scoping is sound (every query filters on claims.Sub, no IDOR vector reachable on add/update/read). ON CONFLICT (cart_id, product_id) merge is genuinely tx-safe and parameterized; SQL is end-to-end parameterized including the bulk DELETE via ANY($2::uuid[]). The recorded pre-existing import cycle is no longer present (CartStoragePort interface lives in package cart so access can implement it without a back-edge; go build ./... passes). Two HIGH issues block the L2 gate: (1) cart.read silently degrades on upstream failure instead of surfacing UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT per TD strict-error-policy, and the errgroup cancellation never fires because catalog goroutines swallow timeouts and inventory goroutine swallows all errors — strict-fan-out contract is violated; (2) CartItemView is missing the contract-mandated `available:bool` + `unavailReason` enum fields (TD response_schema lines 300-301), so the calibration requirement 'never silent fall-through' is broken. MEDIUMs: update-item qty has no upper bound; STOCK_INSUFFICIENT is mapped to 409 instead of TD-required 400 VALIDATION_ERROR; AddItem catalog call has no per-call deadline; remove-item and clear-on-checkout are 501 stubs while their service-layer logic exists wired-but-unreachable. Currency uses float64 (CWE-682) against the cross-cutting int64-minor-units rule. Stubs and contract drift make this a block at L1.

findings.description: cart.read fan-out violates the TD strict-error-policy. Per-item catalog timeouts are swallowed inside each goroutine (line 322-329 returns nil on isUpstreamTimeout) and the inventory goroutine swallows all errors with a slog.Warn (line 340-347 returns nil). Net effect: errgroup cancellation never propagates, and the handler returns 200 SUCCESS with degraded data when TD fan_out_spec.error_policy mandates 'first upstream error from any goroutine cancels all in-flight via errgroup context and surfaces UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT'. Handler_read.go:51-58 has no UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT branch either — every error becomes 500 INTERNAL_ERROR.
findings.recommendation: Return the upstream error from each goroutine (drop the swallow); detect isUpstreamTimeout(err) at handler level and emit 504 UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT per TD error_contract; reserve 500 for genuine DB failures only.

findings.description: CartItemView is missing the contract-mandated `available:bool` and `unavailReason` enum fields (TD response_schema lines 300-301; calibration requirement 'never silent fall-through — always has unavailReason when false'). Code conflates the catalog ProductStatus enum with a pseudo-status "CATALOG_UNREACHABLE" (service.go:326, 371) instead of using the dedicated reason field. Clients cannot distinguish PRODUCT_INACTIVE from OUT_OF_STOCK from CATALOG_UNREACHABLE without parsing the polluted productStatus.
findings.recommendation: Add Available bool `json:"available"` and UnavailReason string `json:"unavailReason"` (enum: "", PRODUCT_INACTIVE, PRODUCT_DELETED, OUT_OF_STOCK, CATALOG_UNREACHABLE). Populate in the enrichment loop in service.go:362-392; keep ProductStatus pure to the catalog enum.

findings.description: updateItemRequest.Qty has only `binding:"min=0"` — no upper bound. addItemRequest correctly uses min=1,max=100 (handler_add_item.go:18). cart_items.qty is INT (32-bit signed); a request with qty=2_147_483_647 passes validation, and if the inventory stock-check returns a high availableQty (or is unreachable in a fail-open path) the value persists. LineSubtotal arithmetic on float64 then accumulates noise.

Stock-insufficient maps to HTTP 409 STOCK_INSUFFICIENT, but TD error_contract for cart.update-item explicitly defines this case as 400 VALIDATION_ERROR with availableQty in detail (td.json line 182). This is contract drift that breaks frontend error parsing keyed on TD-published codes.
findings.recommendation: Map ErrStockInsufficient to HTTP 400 with code VALIDATION_ERROR and the availableQty payload — match the TD failure_codes registry.

findings.description: Service.AddItem calls s.catalog.GetProductDetail(ctx, ...) with the raw request context — no per-upstream deadline. UpdateItem (line 179-180) and ReadCart (line 293-295) wrap context.WithTimeout(fanoutCfg.TimeoutMS). A slow catalog backend on the add-item path can hold the request up to the gateway middleware.Timeout (router.go:35, set to ~10s) instead of the intended 3s upstream budget.
findings.recommendation: Wrap ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, time.Duration(s.fanoutCfg.TimeoutMS)*time.Millisecond) before the catalog call in AddItem; defer cancel().

findings.description: Both handlers return 501 NOT_IMPLEMENTED while Service.RemoveItem (service.go:226-236) and Service.ClearOnCheckout (service.go:405-452) are fully implemented and tested-internal. The router wires the routes (router.go:67-68). Frontend cart-removal flows fail; checkout's CHK-010 cart-clear flow fails post-commit. Calibration: 'could a careful Dev have written this?' — yes, but the missing wire is a 5-line copy of AddItem's pattern; tracked as a latent bug because it breaks two BA acceptance criteria (CART-003, CHK-010).
findings.recommendation: Replace both stubs with handlers that bind/parse, call service.RemoveItem / service.ClearOnCheckout, and map sentinel errors. For clear-on-checkout step 1 must be customerUserId == claims.Sub (AMB-002).

findings.description: CurrentPrice, LineSubtotal, Subtotal are float64. Cross-cutting.pricing.currency rule and TD response_schema state THB minor units as integer. Float arithmetic introduces representation error on accumulation (lineSubtotal += and subtotal +=). For a 50-item cart with mixed prices this can produce off-by-1-satang totals visible to the client.
findings.recommendation: Change all price/subtotal types to int64 minor units; CatalogClient.ProductDetail.CurrentPrice → int64; lineSubtotal := int64(item.Qty) * d.CurrentPrice. Update tests accordingly.

findings.description: Catalog and inventory clients build error strings with raw upstream code and envelope code (e.g. 'catalog: unexpected response code=%d envelope_code=%s'); these flow into wrapper.Respond's Err field on the default branch in every handler. If common/wrapper.Respond echoes Err.Error() into the JSON body, clients learn upstream-service identity and internal envelope codes (information disclosure / fingerprinting).
findings.recommendation: Confirm common/wrapper does NOT serialize Err to body (it should only log). If it does, sanitize: log internally, return only TD-published codes (UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT / INTERNAL_ERROR) to the client.

findings.description: stockMu sync.Mutex protects stockMap, but only the inventory goroutine writes (one writer) and all reads happen after g.Wait() (line 354). The mutex is dead synchronization — no contention is possible. Adds noise without benefit.
findings.recommendation: Drop stockMu; assign stockMap directly inside the inventory goroutine.

findings.description: persistClearIdempotencyNoTx wraps a single INSERT in BeginTx/Rollback/Commit. SaveClearIdempotency could accept the pool directly (or a dbtx interface). Costs one extra round-trip on the no-cart idempotency path.
findings.recommendation: Either let SaveClearIdempotency take an interface satisfied by both pgx.Tx and *pgxpool.Pool, or call pool.Exec directly for the no-cart case.

findings.description: Clients gate on resp.Code != http.StatusOK only — they don't assert resp.Response.Code == app.CodeSuccess. An upstream returning HTTP 200 with an envelope error code would be treated as a valid product detail / stock entry.
findings.recommendation: Assert envelope Code == "SUCCESS" (or app.CodeSuccess) before trusting Data.

findings.description: UpsertItem generates a new UUID on every call (uuid.New() at line 66) even when the row exists and the ON CONFLICT path triggers — the generated ID is discarded. Minor wasted work; not a bug.
findings.recommendation: Move uuid.New() into a CTE or accept that the cost is negligible. Optional polish.

findings.description: INSERT into cart.cart_items uses NOW() in the ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE SET added_at=NOW() — but TD ERD documents added_at as 'NOT reset on merge'. The current code always resets added_at on every merge, contradicting the documented invariant.
findings.recommendation: On CONFLICT, do not update added_at — only update qty. Change to: ON CONFLICT (cart_id, product_id) DO UPDATE SET qty = cart.cart_items.qty + EXCLUDED.qty (drop the added_at line).
